evals.expected_output: Should resolve the handle, orgs and destination from a DevRel section in AGENTS.md (or ask once), work out the previous weekday (Friday on a Monday), fetch that day's involved activity and today's authored items, then ask all four questions in one message: the last posted Today section, what from it actually happened, anything not on GitHub, and today's plan. Only after the answers, output the standup in a fenced text block, describing work in its own words rather than restating PR titles, and never posting it.
expectations: Uses the previous weekday, never a Saturday or Sunday
Asks the four questions in a single message before writing the standup
Includes only work the user confirms; GitHub activity is evidence, not fact
Describes each item in its own words, never restating the PR or issue title
Outputs a copy-ready fenced text block and never posts it

evals.prompt:
Here's yesterday's standup, can you clean it up? 
* fixed the thing in billing #212
* reviewed sarah's pr
* started the docs series
evals.expected_output: Should take the improve-an-existing-daily path: skip fetching GitHub and the questions, and reformat only what was given. Should rewrite each line as a clear sentence, keep links the user gave, expand only where there's evidence of parts, and not invent activity, numbers or sub-steps.
expectations: Doesn't fetch GitHub or ask the four questions
Rewrites only the items given, without inventing work or sub-steps
Keeps the format: fenced text block, bullets of at most two lines

evals.prompt: /daily-standup 2026-11-20 and post it to Slack for me
evals.expected_output: Should report on 20 November as given, gather activity and ask the four questions, then output the standup in a fenced block for the user to paste — declining to post it to Slack, since the command never posts.
expectations: Uses the given date instead of the previous weekday
Declines to post to Slack and outputs the standup for the user to paste
